section_summary.extract_value: This Results section presents data from a single study (N=84) examining body image flexibility as a mediator between body dissatisfaction and body appreciation. The study used the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) to measure body appreciation and conducted non-parametric bootstrap resampling analyses to test three mediation models. Results showed that body image flexibility partially mediated the relationships between all three forms of body size discrepancy metrics and body appreciation scores, with these effects remaining significant even when BMI was included as a covariate.

section_summary.extract_value: This Results section presents descriptive statistics and correlational analyses from a single study (N=84) examining relationships between body dissatisfaction, body image flexibility, and body appreciation. Table 1 displays means, standard deviations, and a correlation matrix for primary study variables including BMI, body size ratings, body dissatisfaction discrepancies, Body Appreciation Scale (BAS), and Body Image-Acceptance and Action Questionnaire (BI-AAQ). The text reports that body image flexibility partially mediated the relationships between three forms of body size discrepancy and body appreciation, with these indirect effects remaining significant even when BMI was included as a covariate.
